diagnosis: Across all 4 rollouts, every decisive fact (PF1, PF2, PF3, PF4) was properly revealed by its owner via reveal actions. This caused C8 and P1 to fail in those three rollouts. Rollout 2 was the sole rollout that cited PF1–PF4 in justification_fact_ids, passing C8 and P1, but it failed C6 due to an ENCODING MISMATCH: the top-level decisions.menu_item was set to "60 sandwiches" instead of "sandwiches" (the offer_records.A5.menu_item was correctly "sandwiches"). No rollouts hit the turn cap; all settled in 6–11 turns.

fix_instructions: The primary driver is REVEALED BUT UNUSED for C8 and P1 across rollouts 0, 1, and 3. Fix the settlement norm/template for A1 so that when a decisive fact has been revealed via a reveal action, its fact_id must appear in justification_fact_ids and credited_facts — the agent already uses the values correctly in offer_records but fails to attribute them. Add an explicit instruction in A1's shared_context or settle-eligibility condition requiring that every revealed PF fact be cited in justification_fact_ids before settling. Secondary: fix C6's ENCODING MISMATCH in rollout 2 by making the check tolerant of the top-level decisions.menu_item field containing a quantity-prefixed string (e.g., "60 sandwiches"), or alternatively tighten the settlement template to enforce that decisions.menu_item must contain only the bare menu item name ("sandwiches"), matching the offer_records format. The C6 fix should align the check's expected value with how the model naturally encodes the winning vendor's menu item at the top level versus in offer_records.
